shape.name: Shape F - Productive Skills (Speaking)
shape.description: Regular speaking lesson that moves students from recalling the reading-crisis evidence through free, structured debate. After finishing the final chunk of the reading pack using the reciprocal-teaching method they already know, students revise the Open - Your view - Respond - Resolution discussion structure, then run two speed-dating rounds: first with structured cue cards (Set A) that scaffold the discussion and provide target language, then with bare topic cards (Set B) that give only a prompt. The lesson closes with an open-class reflection on the single most useful lesson for the exam.
shape.pedagogical_justification: Speed dating is a structured speaking fluency technique in which students rotate partners at a fixed interval, maximising the number of interlocutors each learner speaks with and reducing the pressure of speaking to the whole class. Scaffolding is staged down: the first round provides both a discussion structure and functional language cues, and the second removes the scaffold so students must deploy the structure independently - a retrieval-style release matching the exam demand. The premise (debating issues, trying to reach compromise) develops argumentation and disagreement-management that feed directly into the speaking exam.
shape.main_aim_format: By the end of the lesson, learners will have debated argument topics in a speed-dating format, using the Open - Your view - Respond - Resolution structure and working towards compromise with a partner.

example_lesson_plan.header:
Objective:
By the end of the lesson, learners will have debated a series of argument topics in a speed-dating format, using the Open - Your view - Respond - Resolution discussion structure and working towards compromise.
Teacher:
Ed Rush
Date:
2 September, 2026
Duration:
46 minutes
CEFR Level:
B1
Lesson Shape:
Shape F - Productive Skills (Speaking)
Materials:
The Reading Crisis: Why Fluency Matters More Than Ever (adapted from OECD, Thai Enquirer, Edutopia and PIAAC research); reading pack (4 chunks); Harvard expert video on the reading decline (bare reference); structured cue cards Set A; bare topic cue cards Set B
Assessment:
Observation of structured and free debate; open-class reflection
Skills:
Speaking

stages.stage_aim: To activate prior knowledge of the reading-crisis evidence
procedure: Whole-class recall: ask Ss what the Harvard expert warned about the reading crisis (bare reference to the video watched in the reading lesson - no transcript).
Elicit the chain: a reduction in reading is widening the gap in reading scores.
Elicit the three causes of the reduction in reading: declining test accountability, social media use, and absenteeism.
One or two Ss restate the chain aloud so everyone hears the key argument before the debate.

stages.stage_aim: To finish the reading pack using the established reciprocal-teaching method
procedure: Remind Ss of the four reciprocal-teaching roles: Predictor, Clarifier, Questioner, Summariser.
Groups rotate roles one final position for Chunk 4: Thailand's fall is sharpest.
Read silently, then each student performs their final role.
Each group agrees a single-sentence summary of the whole reading pack.

stages.stage: Set up the debate and revise structure
stages.stage_aim: To introduce the debate topic, revise the discussion structure and stress compromise
procedure: Introduce the main argument topic (education-themed argument prompts).
Revise the discussion structure together: Open - Your view - Respond - Resolution.
Stress that most issues CAN be debated and there is no single correct answer; the aim is to try to reach a compromise.
Model one short debate with the class, aiming for a compromise.
Ss practise the structure once in pairs.

stages.stage_aim: To set the protocol for the speed-dating rounds
procedure: Re-explain speed dating: Ss sit opposite a partner; on the signal they discuss, then one row rotates.
Clarify each round: 30 seconds silent prep (no notes), then 2 minutes of discussion.
Confirm the goal each round: state your opinion, listen, respond, and work towards a compromise.

stages.stage: Speed debate - structured cue cards (Set A)
stages.stage_aim: To debate five structured topics with discussion and language support
procedure: Hand out the structured cue cards (Set A): five education topics with the discussion structure and target language cues.
30 seconds silent prep per round (no notes).
2-minute discussion per round using Open - Your view - Respond - Resolution and the target language cues.
Rotate after each round; five rounds covering the five structured topics.
Teacher circulates, notes language, and encourages Ss to work towards compromise.

stages.stage: Speed debate - bare topic cue cards (Set B)
stages.stage_aim: To debate five topics with no scaffold, deploying the structure independently
procedure: Hand out the bare topic cue cards (Set B): five prompts only, no structure or language support.
30 seconds silent prep per round (no notes).
2-minute discussion per round; Ss must supply the structure themselves.
Rotate after each round; five rounds covering the five bare topics.
Teacher observes whether Ss can run the discussion structure without the scaffold.

stages.stage_aim: To consolidate the most transferable lesson for the exam
procedure: Whole-class discussion: what is the single most important thing you learned today that will help you in the exam?
Invite several Ss to share one idea and one reason.
Elicit a takeaway about structure, compromise, or handling disagreement - the ideas that transfer to the speaking exam.

materials: The Reading Crisis: Why Fluency Matters More Than Ever - adapted from OECD, Thai Enquirer, Edutopia and PIAAC research
Reading pack (4 chunks): Reading at 15, Reading pays, Reading can be learned, Thailand's fall
Harvard expert video on the reading decline (bare reference - viewed in the reading lesson, no transcript)
Structured cue cards Set A: five education topics (discussion structure + target language cues)
Bare topic cue cards Set B: five topics (prompt only)
metadata.main_aim: By the end of the lesson, learners will have debated argument topics in a speed-dating format, using the Open - Your view - Respond - Resolution discussion structure and working towards compromise with a partner.
metadata.subsidiary_aim: To recall the evidence and causes of the reading decline from the reading-crisis pack, and to use discussion language to state an opinion, agree, disagree and propose compromise.
